title: Alaska Airlines 1866
summary: Alaska Airlines Flight 1866, a Boeing 727, was conducting an instrument approach to Juneau Airport on a localizer directional aid (LDA) approach. The crew received erroneous navigation radio indications suggesting they were closer to the airport than their actual position. The aircraft descended below obstacle clearance altitude and struck a mountain slope in the Chilkat range 18.5 miles west of the airport at approximately 2,500 feet altitude, killing all 111 occupants.
probable_cause: Display of misleading navigational information concerning the flight's progress along the localizer course which resulted in premature descent below obstacle clearance altitude. The origin of the erroneous navigational information could not be determined. Contributing factors were the crew's failure to use all available navigational aids to check progress along the localizer and failure to perform required audio identification of navigation facilities.

factors.evidence: Captain's navigation radio presented crew with consistently false information at several points along approach path; specific reason for erroneous indications could not be determined (p. 2, Synopsis)
Crew did not use audio identification features of navigation radios; crew did not use all available navigational aids to check flight's progress along localizer (p. 2, Synopsis)
Crew descended below safe altitude based on erroneous position reports from navigation system (p. 2)
Aircraft struck slope in Chilkat Mountain range at approximately 2,500 feet level, 18.5 miles west of Juneau Airport, approximately on inbound localizer course (p. 2)

events.text: Controller issued clearance to descend at pilots discretion to cross PLEASANT at 10,000 feet (p. 3, History of Flight)
Crew reported leaving FL230 descending to 10,000 feet at PLEASANT intersection (p. 3)
Controller instructed stop descent at 12,000 feet due to other traffic near Juneau (p. 3)
Crew reported passing PLEASANT and entering holding pattern (p. 3)
Crew cleared for LDA approach to Runway 8 and reported passing final approach fix at Barlow Intersection, 10.2 nautical miles west of airport (p. 2, 3)
Crew descended based on erroneous navigation radio indications suggesting closer proximity to airport than actual position (p. 2, 3)
Aircraft struck slope in Chilkat Mountain range at approximately 2,500-foot level, 18.5 miles west of Juneau Airport (p. 2, 3)
Aircraft destroyed by impact; isolated post-crash fires occurred; all 104 passengers and 7 crew fatally injured (p. 2)

recommendations.text: Amend public instrument approach procedure for LDA approach to Juneau, Alaska, Airport to reflect addition of Distance Measuring Equipment (DME) as source of determining location of fixes on final approach course of localizer

safety_changes: Addition of DME equipment to LDA approach procedure for Juneau Airport

notes: Read sections: Synopsis (p. 2), Probable Cause (p. 2-3), History of Flight (p. 3)
Navigation radio failure cause never determined per NTSB investigation
Crew failed to use audio ident verification per report
All 111 occupants killed in CFIT with mountain terrain at 2,500 feet altitude
NTSB Recommendation A-72-14 addressing navigational aid requirements
